title: LifeYoda private horizon config
description: Long-horizon layer. One terminal goal, the periods it spans, the hard deadlines that cannot move, and the tracks whose milestones are derived backwards from that goal. Read-only for every workflow that consumes it.

terminalGoal.description: The single fixed point every milestone is derived backwards from. Exactly one.

label.description: What the terminal goal is, in plain words.

date.description: Date of the terminal goal, YYYY-MM-DD. Distance to this date is what turns a plan into a countdown.

terms.description: Named periods the horizon spans. They supply the background rhythm: stretches that free up time and stretches that consume it.

hardDeadlines.description: Dates that cannot be moved by rescheduling. Each carries a confidence level and, where relevant, the milestones it blocks.

tracks.description: Parallel lines of work competing for the same weeks. Weights across tracks are the basis for the weekly time budget.

cadence.description: Recurring review points that keep the horizon honest between milestones.

weeklyReview.description: When the weekly horizon review happens, e.g. a weekday name.

monthlyReview.description: When the monthly sync with the person who owns the terminal goal happens, e.g. 'first week of each month'.

lookaheadDays.description: How many days ahead a consuming workflow surfaces milestones. Overrides horizon.lookaheadDays in config/public.defaults.json.

end.description: Last day of instruction, YYYY-MM-DD. Exams usually fall after this.

examStart.description: First day of the final exam period, YYYY-MM-DD.

examEnd.description: Last day of the final exam period, YYYY-MM-DD.

breaks.description: Holidays and recesses inside the term. A single-day break has start equal to end.

source.description: Where these dates came from, so a stale term can be re-checked against the same place.

end.description: Last day off, YYYY-MM-DD. Equal to start for a single day.

id.description: Stable identifier, referenced from milestone dependsOn and from the blocks list of another deadline.

label.description: What is due on that date.

source.description: Where the date was read from, so it can be re-checked. Expected on anything marked VERIFIED.

confidence.description: VERIFIED: read from an authoritative published source. DERIVED: not published anywhere, computed backwards from other constraints, and therefore must carry a companion milestone that confirms it with whoever can make it real. INFERRED: guessed from a pattern such as last year's date, and never presented as settled.

blocks.description: Ids of milestones or other hard deadlines that cannot happen until this one is met.

id.description: Short stable identifier, used as the argument that expands this one track.

label.description: Human-readable name of this line of work.

weightPct.description: Share of the working week this track should get. Weights across all tracks are expected to sum to 100; a dormant track sits at 0 and draws from another track's share once it wakes up.

milestones.description: Points of completion for this track. Dates are derived backwards from the terminal goal, not forwards from today.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across every track. Referenced by dependsOn and by a hard deadline's blocks list.

label.description: What finishing this milestone means, specific enough to name the artifact it produces.

targetDate.description: Date this should be done by, YYYY-MM-DD. A target date in the past with a status other than done is a slip, and gets surfaced as one.

dependsOn.description: Ids of milestones or hard deadlines that must complete first. The critical path is the longest chain of these. Must stay acyclic.

status.description: planned: not started. in_progress: underway. done: finished. slipped: past its target date and still unfinished. blocked: waiting on something outside this milestone's control.

evidence.description: What proves this is done, or the constraint that fixes its date. Free text, and the place to record a rule such as a daily time cap or a fallback input.

notionPageId.description: Id of the tracker row mirroring this milestone, when one exists. Optional: the horizon file stays readable without it.
